comments.note: _normaliseType() in components.js does not HTML-escape the type parameter before interpolating it into the class attribute value. A type value containing '"' would break the attribute quoting. For all current callers (programmatic status strings: READY, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETE, etc.) this is not exploitable — the values never contain HTML special characters. Not a regression vs. the old statusBadge, which had the same trait. Low-risk; recommend adding escapeHtml() on the normType in a future hardening pass if type ever comes from user input.

UI.badge(null, 'label') produces 'label' (empty class suffix). All real callers guard against null/undefined status upstream, so this is not a practical concern. The existing statusBadge already short-circuits on falsy status with 'if (!status) return \'\''.
